pages.heading: Advisors had everything in one place. Except retirement.
lines: At XP Inc., one of Brazil's largest investment brokers, advisors run their day in HUB. Retirement was the exception: it still lived in **Connect**, an older platform.
**Client:** XP Inc.
**My role:** Product Designer
**Team:** with Jaqueline Manso (Product Designer)
**Platform:** HUB, XP's web platform for advisors
**Timeline:** Oct 2021 – Apr 2022

pages.heading: The problem: a product left behind
lines: Connect had a confusing structure and dated components. It slowed advisors down, created support tickets and kept retirement apart from the rest of HUB.
The brief: move every retirement operation into HUB, and improve each journey on the way. We'd know it worked if we saw:
- fewer support tickets
- happier advisors
- more pension assets under custody via HUB
- more advisors using HUB, more often

items.body: Moving money between pension plans: into XP from elsewhere (external), or within XP (internal).
Money paid into a plan: a first deposit, a one-off top-up or a monthly amount.
Taking money out of a pension plan, in part or in full.
Brazil's two kinds of private pension. Taxed differently, each suits a different client.
Two ways a plan can be taxed when money comes out, each with its own restrictions.
Plans are run by insurers (XP Seguros, Icatu, SulAmérica…), each with its own rules.

pages.heading: Start where it hurts most
lines: Retirement in Connect covered many operations: portability, contributions, withdrawals, beneficiary changes and more. Stakeholders wanted them all in HUB by Q2 2022.
We started with **portability**, external and internal. It had the most complaints, the most business rules and the most technical effort.
Each discovery started the same way: business, operations and tech together, looking at volumes, support tickets and the main pain points.

variants.label: Before · Connect
variants.note: Connect asked for the destination insurer first, then led into one long form.

variants.label: After · HUB
variants.note: HUB starts from the plans: pick one, choose what to do (external or internal portability, or a new investment), then go step by step.

pages.heading: Discovery: rules on top of rules
lines: Portability is complex. Every insurer working with XP has its own rules, payment methods and data to collect, and portability between XP plans works differently again.
PGBL and VGBL plans add tax restrictions on top, depending on the plan's tax table.
The open question was whether advisors themselves understood all these differences, and how the product could help them.

items.title: Destination first was confusing.
items.body: Connect's very first step was choosing the destination insurer, before anything else.

items.title: One plan at a time.
items.body: A portability couldn't start from more than one origin plan.

items.title: External or internal?
items.body: Advisors and clients didn't understand how each kind of portability is requested.

items.title: Too many fields.
items.body: The forms asked for lots of registration data that wasn't needed.

items.title: Words that didn't help.
items.body: “Intracorretora” portability or “internal transfer”? The terms caused confusion.

pages.heading: From pain points to bets
lines: We grouped the pain points, studied the business rules and limits, and drew a blueprint of the journey, comparing Connect with HUB.
Each opportunity became a hypothesis with a clear upside and a clear risk. We ranked them by support volume, technical feasibility and fit with the business goals.
The boldest one: letting advisors start from a **list of funds** instead of a client. Nothing like it existed in Connect.

items.title: Start from the fund list
items.body: Begin from the plans available, not the client. The upside: faster search and room to grow. The risk: nothing like it existed in Connect.

items.title: Keep the client search
items.body: For existing plans and everything tied to a client, keep the client-first path advisors already knew.

items.title: Use the advisors' words
items.body: Find out which terms advisors actually use for each kind of portability, and name things that way.

items.title: Teach inside the flow
items.body: Bring insurer rules, tax tables and plan details into the journey itself, instead of piling up disclaimers.

pages.heading: Saying it the advisor's way
lines: Connect called the same thing by different names, and advisors didn't always know which was which.
So we tested the words too, as part of the research with advisors.
In HUB, each option also carries a one-line description, so the name never has to do all the work.

poll.title: What would you call it?
poll.question: An advisor wants to move a client's money from one XP pension plan to another. Which name would they look for?
poll.reveal: Most advisors knew internal portability as “Intracorretora”, the word they'd used for years.
poll.prompt: Pick one to see what advisors said.

pages.heading: Testing with advisors
lines: We validated the refined prototype with advisors of different experience levels, in two waves.
**Concept test:** 5 semi-structured interviews about the new flow, the terms and how clear the first steps were.
**Usability test:** a Maze test sent to about 430 advisors. 46 completed it, with three tasks: start a portability, choose the origin plan and finish the flow.
We measured task success, drop-off and satisfaction after each task (ASQ).

funnel.title: Who took part
funnel.note: Plus 5 in-depth interviews with advisors of different experience levels.

pages.heading: Habit, or a usability problem?
lines: Most of the flow passed, with small fixes. One part split opinions: starting a new plan from the **fund list**.

Advisors were used to starting from the origin plan, as in Connect, and one said in Maze it felt more logical. In an interview, another saw value in the fund list but was thrown at first, out of habit.
Task success was still 90%. So was it a usability problem, or years of Connect? With 46 testers, we couldn't be sure.

variants.label: Start from a fund
variants.note: New: browse the plans available, compare them, and start a new investment or a portability.

variants.label: Start from a client
variants.note: Familiar: find the client, see their plans and act on them.

pages.heading: Letting the pilot decide
lines: The roadmap had to keep moving, so instead of holding the release, we built the answer into it.

The four offices that run the most portabilities used the new flow for real, with weekly sessions to present it, train advisors and collect feedback. Advisors were split into Beta and non-Beta groups, and feedback came in through Medallia.
The answer: the fund list was validated. Advisors got used to it and agreed it made sense for the product.

timeline.title: From a pilot to every office

pages.heading: Moving house, one room at a time
lines: We started in October 2021. By April 2022, **92%** of retirement features had been built into HUB, and the number of offices using it kept growing.
Initial Contribution reused the same navigation as portability. Tested with 150 advisors, it reached an **80%** task success rate.
Feedback praised the speed, the ease of use and how clear the navigation was.

items.text: Every migration I ran went absolutely smoothly and was easy to do.
Lots of products, and a very easy portability system.
Signing up and portability are easy to understand.
The pension portability process is excellent: quick and practical for both advisor and client.
I had the chance to request a portability to XP, and it was simple and quick. Congratulations on the efficiency.
A fast portability process, easy to run, with competitive funds available.

showcase.title: The final result
intro: Retirement now lives where advisors already work: a fund list to start from, client positions to act on, and guided steps for each operation.
